column1: # FORMAT: four TAB-separated columns, `A <op> B <why>`, where <op> is one of
# `<`, `=`, `>` - deliberately `apk version -t`'s own output vocabulary, so
# that the follow-up live differential named in the comparator's header (run
# `apk version -t A B` per row on a networked box with apk-tools installed)
# is a direct column diff rather than a translation.  Whole-line `#` comments
# and blank lines are ignored, matching the record-format instinct the rest
# of this repository uses; a value never needs escaping because no column can
# PROVENANCE, STATED PLAINLY.  Every row here is DERIVED from apk-tools'
# documented version grammar and suffix ordering (report.md §2.5) and from
# the specific cases report.md §2.4/§2.5 name.  NONE of it was harvested by
# running `apk version -t`: scoursh is egress-restricted and the development
# host has no `apk` binary, so a live 30k-pair harvest of the shape
# `modules/sca/semver.sh` used for npm was not available.  This is the
# strongest OFFLINE corpus available and it is not a substitute for that run
# - see the comparator's own "THE OFFLINE-CORPUS LIMIT" section for the
# follow-up hardening this owes, and for the two rows (the fractional
# components, and `1.0 < 1.0-r0`) to scrutinise first when it happens.
# The suite asserts the MIRROR of every row too (`A < B` implies `B > A`) and
# the reflexivity of every distinct version, so a comparator that returned a
# constant could not pass by agreeing with one column.
